description: Our goal is to change the conventional perception of crop-farming operations and to explore how this sector can be developed and improved for the benefit of our farmers.
summary:
TerraScan is a web tool that helps farmers decide what, when and how much to sow. Farmers often make these decisions without knowing how weather and soil will behave on their specific field.

TerraScan lets the user outline a field on a satellite map and turns NASA data into a clear diagnosis. Using a year of NASA POWER (MERRA-2) and GPM IMERG data, plus MODIS NDVI, SRTM terrain and SoilGrids soil properties, it shows the risks of water deficit, heat, frost, heavy rain, dry soil, erosion and waterlogging. The field is split into zones, each with its own terrain and risk values.

The user then sets their priorities and compares three crop rotations, with a transparent view of what each result rests on and which data is missing. Finally, TerraScan produces a work calendar with seeding rates, fertilizer, water and expected yield, and saves everything to a personal history.

By making NASA Earth observation data understandable and actionable for farmers, TerraScan supports better planning, more efficient use of water and inputs, and lower climate risk.
details:
TerraScan is a web tool that helps farmers make sowing decisions under uncertain weather and soil conditions. The user outlines a field on a satellite map, and TerraScan turns NASA data into a clear diagnosis and plan.

It uses a year of NASA POWER (MERRA-2) and GPM IMERG data to assess water deficit, heat, frost, heavy rain, dry soil and waterlogging. MODIS NDVI shows “bare” periods, SRTM terrain data gives slope and erosion risk, and SoilGrids provides water retention. The field outline is split into zones, each with its own terrain-based risks.

The user then sets priorities, compares three crop rotations side by side, and receives a work calendar with seeding rates, fertilizer, water and expected yield. Plans are saved to a personal history.

Built with HTML, CSS and JavaScript, Leaflet for maps, and deployed on Vercel. Scores are approximate guides to be refined with FAO-56, RUSLE and TWI methods.
dataRefs: NASA POWER API (T2M temperature, precipitation, humidity, GWETROOT soil moisture)
MERRA-2 Reanalysis (root-zone soil wetness via POWER)
GPM IMERG (daily precipitation, IMERG_PRECTOT via POWER)
projectRefs: SoilGrids by ISRIC (250 m soil properties)
Open Topo Data (elevation API serving SRTM 30 m)
Open-Meteo Elevation API (Copernicus DEM 90 m, fallback)
FAO-56 Crop Evapotranspiration guidelines (water deficit method)
